claim: Two brain aging patterns were identified among 37,013 healthy participants from UK Biobank using a data-driven approach that incorporates both cross-sectional changes and longitudinal trajectories of structural brain aging.
source: In this investigation, we present a data-driven approach that incorporate both cross-sectional changes and longitudinal trajectories of structural brain aging and identified two brain aging patterns among 37,013 healthy participants from UK Biobank.
evidence: The study directly reports the identification of two brain aging patterns from analysis of UK Biobank data.

claim: Participants with accelerated brain aging demonstrated accelerated biological aging.

claim: The 'last in, first out' mirroring hypothesis between brain aging and brain development was validated.
source: Further, by integrating longitudinal neuroimaging studies from a multi-center adolescent cohort, we validated the 'last in, first out' mirroring hypothesis and identified brain regions with manifested mirroring patterns between brain aging and brain development.
evidence: The study reports validation of this hypothesis using longitudinal neuroimaging data.

claim: Brain regions with manifested mirroring patterns between brain aging and brain development were identified.
source: Further, by integrating longitudinal neuroimaging studies from a multi-center adolescent cohort, we validated the 'last in, first out' mirroring hypothesis and identified brain regions with manifested mirroring patterns between brain aging and brain development.

claim: Genomic analyses revealed risk loci and genes contributing to accelerated brain aging.
source: Genomic analyses revealed risk loci and genes contributing to accelerated brain aging and delayed brain development, providing molecular basis for elucidating the biological mechanisms underlying brain aging and related disorders.

claim: Structural brain alterations intimately link brain development and brain aging.
source: The structure of the brain undergoes continual changes throughout the entire lifespan, with structural brain alterations intimately linking brain development and brain aging (Fjell and Walhovd, 2010; Shaw et al., 2008).

claim: Brain aging is a progressive process that often co-occurs with biological aging.
source: Brain aging is a progressive process that often co-occurs with biological aging and declines of cognitive functions (Elliott et al., 2021; Mattson and Arumugam, 2018; Park and Reuter-Lorenz, 2009), which contribute to the onset and acceleration of neurodegenerative (Mariani et al., 2005) and neuropsychiatric disorders (Kaufmann et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: 18,929 (51.1%) participants had the first brain aging pattern characterized by higher total GMV at baseline and a slower rate of GMV decrease over time.

claim: Cortical gray matter volume (GMV) from 33 regions in each hemisphere were generated using Desikan–Killiany Atlas.
source: Briefly, cortical gray matter volume (GMV) from 33 regions in each hemisphere were generated using Desikan–Killiany Atlas (Desikan et al., 2006), and total gray matter volume (TGMV), intracranial volume (ICV) and subcortical volume were derived from ASEG atlas (Fischl et al., 2002 See Appendix 1—table 3).
evidence: This describes the data processing methodology with citation to the atlas used.

claim: Total gray matter volume (TGMV), intracranial volume (ICV) and subcortical volume were derived from ASEG atlas.
source: Briefly, cortical gray matter volume (GMV) from 33 regions in each hemisphere were generated using Desikan–Killiany Atlas (Desikan et al., 2006), and total gray matter volume (TGMV), intracranial volume (ICV) and subcortical volume were derived from ASEG atlas (Fischl et al., 2002 See Appendix 1—table 3).
evidence: This describes the data processing methodology with citation to the atlas used.

claim: The first 15 principal components explaining approximately 70% of the total variations of regional GMV deviation were used in multivariate k-means clustering.
source: Deviation of regional GMV from the population average was calculated for each participant at age 60 years and dimensionality reduction was conducted via principal component analysis (PCA). The first 15 principal components explaining approximately 70% of the total variations of regional GMV deviation were used in multivariate k-means clustering.
evidence: This describes the analytical methodology used in the study.

claim: PhenoAge was developed as an aging biomarker incorporating composite clinical and biochemical data.
source: Next, we examined PhenoAge, which was developed as an aging biomarker incorporating composite clinical and biochemical data (Levine et al., 2018), and observed higher PhenoAge among participants with brain aging pattern 2 compared to pattern 1 (p=0.019, Cohen's D=0.027).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to previous research.
